parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime splits sharply by layer. National entry is a universal exposure: the 2025 executive order forces birth-sex markers on national documents, the foreign-ministry cable instructs officers to refuse cases with document/sex discrepancies and contemplate lifetime fraud bars, and foreign governments now issue trans-specific travel advisories after documented detentions of visitors. If a visitor falls into national custody, documented abuse (forced labour, sexual violence, hormone withdrawal in corrections/immigration detention) is severe. But within this state/province — the operative environment for the visit itself — the record documents working protections: a 2020 civil-rights statute covering public accommodations, hate-crime coverage, panic-defence repeal, X-marker licences, no facility ban, and a 2026 risk assessment placing it in the low-risk group with youth policies unlikely to extend to adults. No imprisonment pathway exists for the visitor in this state; severity concentrates at the national border and custody, mitigated by the state's operating protections.

entry_documents.exposure: Documented national exposure: passport regime restricted to birth-sex markers, February 2025 cable directs officers to refuse applicants with sex-document discrepancies and consider permanent fraud ineligibility; visitors from other countries have been detained over visa issues; X passports risk confiscation/blocked processing.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry; fraud findings require four elements and are never automatic; litigation ongoing; legal-aid FAQ exists.
entry_documents.interaction: Border exposure precedes any state protection: a discrepancy triggers federal adjudication before the visitor reaches the protective state layer.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented national custody harm: corrections bureau conversion-style policies, hormone withdrawal; immigration custody forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement, severe sexual abuse of trans men; reporting transparency ended 2025.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Several executive orders enjoined in court; hate-crime statute national.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any state-level friction that escalates to federal custody (visa/fraud allegation) moves the traveller into the abusive national custody system.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars congruent facilities in federally funded single-sex facilities; national scan shows criminalised facility use in 4 states/provinces with a documented arrest. Not operative in this state/province.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This state/province has no facility ban; its 2020 public-accommodations statute protects gender identity; X-marker licences since 2020.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State protections govern most everyday facilities; only federally controlled facilities within the state retain the national restriction.

care_services.exposure: Parent-level: proposed national insurance rules bar reimbursement for under-18 care; hospitals subpoenaed for minors' records. Adult visitor care not documented as restricted in this state/province.
care_services.protection: State prohibits providers attempting to change minors' gender identity; broad state civil-rights statute covers services.
care_services.interaction: A travelling minor's care sits under national pressure; adult care locally protected.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Documented state threat-framing at national level: 'radical gender ideology' listed among violent-extremist agendas; counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' groups; removal of LGBT materials; 66% poll support for birth-sex documents.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State hate-crime law, anti-discrimination enforcement, panic-defence repeal operating since 2020-21.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: National demonisation raises outing stakes state-wide, but state institutions are documented as protective, not hostile.

minors_guardians.exposure: Parent: criminal prosecution threatened for teachers facilitating a minor's social transition; national order framing minor care as mutilation; state-level 2023 school bathroom/pronoun policies and February 2025 athletics bar targeted minors.
minors_guardians.protection: Risk assessment finds youth policies unlikely to extend to adults; school policies intended for reversal in 2026 (reversal unconfirmed); state bans conversion of minors.
minors_guardians.interaction: A visiting minor faces school/athletics friction but not adult-targeting; guardian not exposed as facilitator under state law.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Not documented at state/province level; no state/province-specific violence or hate-crime enforcement figures appear; national hate-incident statistics are orientation-aggregate only.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime statute covers gender identity (2020); police response not documented either way.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absence of evidence is not safety, but the state sits in the assessed low-risk group.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Unresolved items: whether 2023 school policies were reversed; referendum date unsourced; identity-document map link dead; adult-extension conclusion is an assessment, not a ruling.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Running legal-aid FAQ on national document rules; state statute, local-option protections and hate-crime law all in force and dated.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Federal litigation outcomes could tighten or loosen the national layer mid-visit; state protections are stable statutory law.

anchor_checks.comparison: Higher than 0.35-A. Vellandra's visitor register excludes and humiliates every trans visitor with no remedy; here the harshest documented national measures (marker rules, fraud-refusal cable) are contested, partially enjoined, and the operative state layer actively protects — exclusion is not the routine outcome.

Above 0.55-B. Kestrel Isles' secondary screening and discretionary refusal resemble the national border friction here, but this jurisdiction adds a protective subnational layer with enforceable accommodations, facility access and hate-crime recourse that 0.55-B lacks.

Roughly comparable, slightly below. 0.75-C documents brief detention, release and workable remedies at the border with no custody-abuse record; here the parent's documented custody abuse, fraud-bar threat and state threat-framing push severity above 0.75-C, offset by stronger in-state protections.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller's journey has two regimes. The national layer imposes universal entry exposure — birth-sex markers, discrepancy-based refusals, possible fraud bars, airport-screening outing, and, if custody occurs, documented severe abuse — which is the heaviest documented feature and prevents any high-band score. But the state/province where the visit occurs is documented as protective and operating: civil-rights statute, hate-crime coverage, X markers, no facility ban, and an independent risk assessment placing it among states unlikely to target trans adults. Consequences of outing within the state are friction and discrimination at worst, not imprisonment. The minor-traveller scenario adds school/athletics friction and national pressure on minor care, but state conversion prohibitions and the assessment against adult extension keep it materially safer. Net: a protective state inside a hostile national entry regime — solidly in the Reduced Risk band, below protection-complete jurisdictions because the border and custody exposures are real, recent and unresolved.
